label: context.reference
description: Arrange event-driven work by inspecting its condition, receiving task and result path.
text:
Use this guide for work that should happen later, repeatedly or in response to an event. Establish the intended action, the condition that should start it and where the result belongs. Use the existing conversation to resolve the intended behavior.

Inspect relevant existing triggers and the interfaces available in this installation. A time schedule, an incoming message, changed data or another event may need different owners. Reuse an arrangement that fits. When it does not, inspect the current contract and source of the relevant owner and adapt or implement the capability within your grant.

Keep triggers discoverable in the client's Triggers view. It lists `cron_life` activations and external event sources with an active receiving checkpoint: World sensors (`interface_type: world`, `role: sensor`, `direction: inbound` or `bidirectional`) and connected applications whose `private_config.task_input_labels` declares what a task receives unprompted, such as incoming mail or messages. Choose a readable source identity and a receiving-task title that describes the action. The client derives their presence from these declarations; there is no separate UI registration. Preserve the source's actual classification; if its arrangement is not represented, identify the missing client support.

Trace the condition through to its consumer. Find the receiving run, the provider or tool that performs the work, and the route that delivers the result. Look for related inputs, outputs, retained state or future templates that must change together. The task-authoring guide describes provider frontier ownership; other owners define their own contracts. Copying a few visible checkpoints does not establish the complete connection.

Check the requested timing against the installed interface's timezone, repetition and next due condition. Use the owner's configuration result for setup and the receiving result when execution is part of the task.

Explain what will happen, under what condition and where the result will appear. Describe the trigger's current state, including whether it is armed or has fired. Save reusable configuration guidance with its applicable conditions.
